tests.name: TEST A: normal close and restart
tests.evidence: logs/xvfb-run1-fresh.log then logs/xvfb-run2-idempotent.log against the same data directory
tests.result: 0 migrations applied on second launch, BSB already present, zero panics

tests.name: TEST C/D: real forced process termination (kill -9) during active runtime, then restart
tests.evidence: logs/xvfb-crash-before-kill.log, then a real SIGKILL sent to the running release binary's actual PID (confirmed exit code 137 = SIGKILL), then logs/xvfb-crash-after-kill-recovery.log
tests.result: real stale -wal/-shm sidecar files confirmed present immediately after the kill; relaunch showed 0 migrations applied, BSB still fully present (0 imported, 31086 already present), zero panics - SQLite's own WAL recovery handled the unclean shutdown transparently

xvfb.note: this is the strongest crash-recovery evidence obtainable without real hardware: a real process, a real uncatchable signal, a real reopen. It is still Environment B (this container), not Environment C (a real pilot machine).

automated.note: structural restart/reconciliation proven by pipeline.rs's file-backed restart tests and the backup/restore round-trip test - see automated-test-summary.json

realHardware.note: a real crash/restart on the actual pilot machine (power loss, OS-level force quit) has not been performed
